anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Row-count, histogram, or correlation statistics are stale, missing, or insufficient, causing systematic cardinality misestimation and sub-optimal execution-plan choices.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Insufficient or degraded network, listener, authentication, or socket resources limit connection establishment and data transfer between clients and the database.

When these two root causes act concurrently, the database can choose overly expensive or chatty execution plans (e.g., large hash joins, full scans, massive result sets) precisely while the network layer is least able to carry the inflated traffic. Observable effects include: • Sharp spikes in query latency and server CPU as misestimated plans over-produce rows. • Prolonged client-side waits during result fetching, intermittent timeouts, and cascading application retries that inflate connection counts. • Server processes stuck in client-read/client-write or network send waits, while execution-plan statistics show grossly inaccurate cardinality estimates. • Frequent plan recompilations after bulk loads that coincide with rising socket backlog, retransmissions, and authentication stalls, making it difficult to pinpoint whether slowness is inside the engine or on the wire.

Causal chain and interaction: Stale or inadequate statistics drive plans that emit far more data than intended or that require excessive remote look-ups, multiplying the volume and duration of network traffic. The bloated data streams saturate already constrained network and listener resources, increasing round-trip latency and connection hold times. In turn, network slow-downs extend query runtimes, delaying automatic statistics refresh jobs, prolonging lock holds on tables undergoing statistics collection, and permitting statistics to drift even further from reality. This feedback loop amplifies both anomalies, leading to widespread throughput collapse, session pile-ups, and unstable performance across transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the amount of time with no network activity after which the operating system should send a TCP keepalive message to the client.
entry.trigger_condition: A TCP client connection has no network activity longer than tcp_keepalives_idle on systems supporting TCP_KEEPIDLE or an equivalent socket option.
entry.workload_impact: Starts TCP keepalive probing for an otherwise idle client connection; together with interval and count settings this can lead to dead connection detection.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
